info.name: grub-media-backend — Manage Roles
info.description:
Full CRUD for permission bundles (roles) and employee assignment.

**Setup:**
1. Import `GrubPac Media - Local.postman_environment.json`
2. Run Login from the Auth collection to populate `accessToken`
3. Run «List Bundles» — copy a bundle id into `{{bundleId}}`
4. Run «List Users in Bundle» — copy a user id into `{{employeeId}}`

**Role rules:**
- `SUPER_ADMIN` — full access to all endpoints
- `ADMIN` — all endpoints EXCEPT modifying a bundle they are currently assigned to (403)
- `EMPLOYEE` — no access (403 on all endpoints)

**Self-edit guard:** An ADMIN cannot PATCH, DELETE, or reassign from a bundle they are assigned to. SUPER_ADMIN bypasses this check.

variable.description: Auto-set by Create Bundle test script; or paste manually from List Bundles
Target employee id for assignment endpoints
Admin user id for admin-assignment endpoints

item.name: Permissions
item.description:
Read and create individual permissions in the catalog.

The catalog ships 36 seeded permissions (5 modules). Custom permissions (`custom: true`) can be added here; they are never overwritten by the seed.

request.description:
Returns all permissions ordered by module → page → action.

Each row: `{ id, module, page, action, label, custom, createdAt }`

✅ 200  array of 36+ permissions
❌ 401  missing / expired token
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Creates a custom permission (`custom: true`). Uses upsert — sending an existing key is a no-op (returns the existing row).

Custom permissions are never wiped by the seed.

✅ 201  the created/existing permission row
❌ 400  missing module / page / action
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

item.name: Bundles
item.description:
CRUD for permission bundles (roles).

Bundles group permissions and are assigned to employees. The seed ships 4 bundles: Viewer (7), HR Manager (11), Content Manager (9), Admin Full Access (36).

request.description:
Returns all bundles with their nested permissions and assigned user count.

Each bundle: `{ id, name, description, createdBy, createdAt, updatedAt, permissions: [...], _count: { users: N } }`

✅ 200  array of bundles ordered by name
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Creates a new bundle. `permissionIds` is an array of `Permission.id` values (get them from «List Permission Catalog»). `createdBy` is set to the caller's id server-side.

The test script saves the new bundle's id as `{{bundleId}}`.

✅ 201  bundle with nested permissions
❌ 400  missing name / invalid permissionIds
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Replaces the bundle's permission set (not a merge — sends the full new list). All three fields are optional; omit a field to leave it unchanged.

`permissionIds` must be non-empty if provided (`@ArrayMinSize(1)`) — sending `[]` returns 400.

Returns `{ bundle, affectedUserCount }` so the UI can show a confirmation dialog before calling.

**Self-edit guard:** An ADMIN cannot PATCH a bundle they are currently assigned to (403). SUPER_ADMIN bypasses.

✅ 200  { bundle: {...}, affectedUserCount: N }
❌ 400  empty permissionIds array
❌ 403  caller is ADMIN assigned to this bundle
❌ 404  bundle not found

Deletes a bundle. `UserBundle` rows for all assigned employees are cascade-deleted. `affectedUserCount` in the response tells you how many employees lost this bundle.

**Self-edit guard:** An ADMIN cannot DELETE a bundle they are currently assigned to (403). SUPER_ADMIN bypasses.

✅ 200  { id, name, affectedUserCount }
❌ 403  caller is ADMIN assigned to this bundle
❌ 404  bundle not found

Returns all non-deleted employees currently holding this bundle, ordered by assignment date.

Each row: `{ userId, bundleId, assignedBy, createdAt, user: { id, firstName, lastName, email, phoneNumber, employeeId, jurisdiction, joiningDate } }`

Soft-deleted users (`deletedAt != null`) are excluded.

✅ 200  array of assignment rows with embedded user
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Bulk-moves employees from the source bundle (`:id`) to a target bundle in a single transaction. Only users actually assigned to the source bundle are moved — userIds not in the source are silently ignored in the validated set (the endpoint throws 400 if none match).

The response `reassigned` count reflects the actual number of rows deleted/created, not the input length.

**Self-edit guard:** An ADMIN cannot reassign from a bundle they are assigned to (403). SUPER_ADMIN bypasses.

✅ 200  { reassigned: N, fromBundleId, targetBundleId }
❌ 400  userIds is empty, or none are in the source bundle
❌ 403  caller is ADMIN assigned to source bundle
❌ 404  source or target bundle not found

item.name: Employee Assignments
item.description: Assign / remove bundles and admin relationships on individual employees.

request.description:
Assigns (or re-assigns) a bundle to an employee. Uses upsert — calling it twice for the same pair updates `assignedBy` only.

✅ 201  UserBundle row
❌ 400  missing bundleId
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Removes a specific bundle from an employee.

✅ 200  the deleted UserBundle row
❌ 404  assignment not found
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Assigns (or replaces) the admin responsible for an employee. Validates that `employeeId` is an `EMPLOYEE` and `adminId` is `ADMIN` or `SUPER_ADMIN`.

Upsert — replaces an existing admin assignment.

✅ 200  AdminEmployeeAssignment row
❌ 404  employee or admin not found / wrong roles
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Removes the admin–employee relationship.

✅ 200  the deleted assignment row
❌ 404  no assignment found
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role

Returns all admin→employee assignments with name/email for both sides.

Each row: `{ employeeId, adminId, assignedBy, createdAt, admin: { id, email, firstName, lastName }, employee: { id, email, firstName, lastName } }`

✅ 200  array
❌ 403  EMPLOYEE role
